newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 13.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN Sydney City Rugby League coach Phil Gould last night declared Brad Fittler would have very little chance of playing for New South Wales in the first State of Origin match on May 28 due to a broken thumb sustained in last Friday's match with St George. Pag 20.

-- Australian national basketball coach Barry Barnes will meet with Melbourne Tigers centre Mark Bradtke next week to discuss his future with the Boomers as they prepares to play Croatia in Melbourne next Tuesday night as part of a five-game series. Page 18

-- The Australian Capital Territory Brumbies will host the Super 12 Rugby Union final at Bruce Stadium later this month if they earn that right by beating Wellington on Sunday. Australian Rugby Union officials have suggested the final be played at the largerSydney Football Stadium, which has double the capacity of Bruce Football Stadium. Page 18.

THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD Australian cricket team captain Mark Taylor's form came under scrutiny from the English press when he faced his opening news conference for the Ashes tour. Taylor thinks his record stands for itself, maintaining there is no need to hand over his captaincy just yet. Page 42.

-- Australian tennis player Jason Stoltenberg defended his title at America's Red Clay championship in Coral Springs, Florida on Sunday by defeating top-seeded Swede Jonas Bjorkman 6-0, 2-6, 7-5. It was Stoltenberg's fourth career tournament win. Page 41.

-- Queensland Rugby Union coach John Connolly yesterday gave the Australian Capital Territory Brumbies several crucial tactical tips on how to overcome the gale-force winds at Athletic Park in Wellington to secure a Super 12 home semi-final berth. Page 41.

THE AGE The Australian Football League has ruled out disciplinary action against Carlton if the clubs' bid to clear Greg Williams of a nine-match suspension fails in the Supreme Court. AFL chief executive Wayne Jackson yesterday rejected suggestions that the Blus would be stripped of the four points won against Richmond on the weekend. Page B10.

-- Australian golfer Greg Norman finished equal fifth behind winner Scott McCarron at the BellSouth Atlanta Classic yesterday. Norman closed to within a stroke of the lead before losing out on a double-bogey at the par-four 17th hole. Page B9.

-- Twenty-two-year old Australian long-distance swimmer Susie Maroney is ahead of schedule in her world-record attempt to become the first person to swim from Cuba to the United States, despite encountering worse-than-expected weather conditions. Page B9.

THE HERALD SUN The Western Bulldogs last night requested that a video charge against vice-captain Chris Grant be brought forward 24-hours so that the case can be heard by the Australian Football League Tribunal tonight when it would not disrupt a vital Wednesday afternon training session. Page 80.

-- The embattled Melbourne AFL team will resist the temptation to accelerate 24-year-old centre half-forward David Shwartz's comeback from his third knee reconstruction following key forward David Neitz's injury during Saturday night's game. Page 78.

-- Horse racing trainer Bart Cummings has announced champion jockey Darren Beadman will replace Gavin Eades to ride Star of Tara in Saturday's Group 1 South Australian Oaks at Morphettville, saying Beadman was his preferred rider whenever he was available. Page 71. --

THE DAILY TELEGRAPH Thanks largely to the efforts of winger Hazem El Masri, who scored four tries last night, the Canterbury Bulldogs thrashed the Mariners 48-36 in a game where defence was at times non-existent. The win confirmed Canterbury's place in the rugby league top five, taking them to equal second with Penrith. Page 64.

-- Newcastle football manager David Morley said yesterday the Knights have proposed that Sunday's match against South Sydney, which was cancelled due to bad weather, be rescheduled to the Australian Rugby League's first Monday night game of the season on Jul 14. Page 61.

-- New South Wales Transport Minister Brian Langton launched the Optus Cup DragonLink yesterday - a scheme for all St George games which provides supporters with return CityRail travel to Carlton station plus entry to home games. The combined rail and groundentry ticket is a first for rugby league and will be available from CityRail stations. Page 61.
